title: OpenAI releases new voice models for more natural live conversations
slides: Why reveal new voice models now, not later?
They adapt tone based on your emotional cues.
But one flaw makes them fail in noisy rooms.
Your app can finally hold live, human-like chats.
Test the model with a real-time stress scenario tomorrow.
thread_text:
1. Why now, not later?

OpenAI rushed the release after a rival leaked similar tech. The demo goes live tomorrow.

2. They read your mood.

The model adjusts tone in real time—angry? It softens. Anxious? It slows down.

3. But noise breaks it.

Background chatter or a door slam causes the model to freeze or repeat words. It can't filter sound yet.

4. Your app talks back.

For the first time, an SDK lets developers embed live, human-like chat into any app. No delays.

5. Test it tomorrow.

Open the demo at 10 AM, simulate a stressful conversation—raised voice, interruptions. Does it hold up?

instagram.caption:
Your app can now host live, human-like voice chats—and it adjusts its tone to how you sound.

OpenAI just released new voice models, rushed after a rival leaked similar tech. The model softens its voice if you sound angry, slows down if you’re anxious. But background noise (a door slam, chatter) still makes it freeze or repeat words.

For creators and app developers: this is the first SDK that lets you embed live, conversational voice without delays. 🎙️

Test it tomorrow at 10 AM: simulate a stressful talk—raised voice, interruptions. Does it keep up? 🧠
